mainTopic: מגילה ט״ז ע״א: מדרשים על אסתר פרקים ו׳–ז׳: כבוד מרדכי, השפלת המן, הסעודה ומפלתו
overview: This amud continues the גמרא's line-by-line reading of מגילת אסתר, chapters 6 and 7. It opens with the record of מרדכי's good deed: שמשי kept erasing it and גבריאל kept rewriting it, and רבי שילא learns from this, by קל וחומר, that Heaven's record of ישראל's merits can never be erased. The גמרא then tells a long story of המן carrying out the king's order. He tries to dodge it, finds מרדכי teaching הלכות קמיצה, and is forced to bathe מרדכי, cut his hair, and bend down so he can climb onto the horse. On the parade route, המן's daughter mistakenly dumps filth on her own father and then falls to her death, which explains why המן went home 'mourning and with his head covered.' המן's advisors are called 'wise' for warning that the Jews rise to the stars, so his fall would be total. At אסתר's feast, the גמרא shows heaven working behind the scenes: a מלאך pushes אסתר's hand toward המן, and מלאכים uproot the king's trees in המן's name and push המן onto the couch. חרבונה is revealed as a former partner of המן who switched sides, and the doubled word שככה is explained as two angers calming together. The amud ends by starting a question about יוסף giving בנימין extra clothes, which continues on the next amud.

steps.title: שמשי Erases and גבריאל Rewrites
steps.stepSummary: The end of an answer that began on the previous amud. The פסוק says the record was "כתוב" (being written) instead of "כתב" (written), because it was erased and rewritten again and again.
steps.simpleTranslation: [This teaches] that שמשי was erasing and גבריאל was writing.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא is finishing its answer to a wording question on the previous amud. The question was why the פסוק uses the present-sounding word "כתוב" for something written long ago.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The answer is that the record of מרדכי saving the king was being written again and again. שמשי, the king's scribe who hated the Jews, kept erasing it, and the angel גבריאל kept writing it back. That is why the פסוק describes it as still being written.

keyTerms.meaning: The king's scribe, an enemy of the Jews (see עזרא ד׳)

steps.confusionAlert: This line starts in the middle of a sentence. The question it answers ("why כתוב and not כתב?") appears on the previous amud.

phrases.english: that Shimshai was erasing and Gavriel was writing.
phrases.notes: This wraps up the answer that started on the previous amud: "[It teaches] that..."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Finishes the answer to the wording question earlier (כתוב versus כתב).
steps.terutzResolutionType: Explains an unusual word by pointing to an ongoing event.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The word כתוב seems odd for something written in the past.
steps.terutzMaskana: כתוב shows the record was being rewritten repeatedly after being erased.

steps.title: A קל וחומר About Writing That Cannot Be Erased
steps.stepSummary: רבי אסי quotes רבי שילא: writing down here that benefits ישראל could not be erased, so writing in Heaven certainly cannot.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אסי said: רבי שילא of the village of תמרתא taught: If writing below that is for the merit of ישראל cannot be erased, then writing above (in Heaven) surely cannot be erased.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אסי brings a teaching from רבי שילא that builds a lesson on the story just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The story showed that even an earthly book, the king's record, could not have מרדכי's merit erased from it. רבי שילא uses a קל וחומר to go further. If that is true of a human book, a Heavenly record of ישראל's merits certainly cannot be wiped away.

keyTerms.meaning: All the more so; the closing words of a קל וחומר

steps.whyThisMatters: It turns a detail of the מגילה story into a lasting comfort: the merits of ישראל recorded in Heaven are permanent.

phrases.english: Rabbi Asi said:

phrases.aramaic: דָּרֵשׁ רַבִּי שֵׁילָא אִישׁ כְּפַר תְּמַרְתָּא:
phrases.english: Rabbi Sheila, a man of the village of Timarta, expounded:
If writing that is below,
which is for the merit of the Jewish people,
cannot be erased,
writing that is above, all the more so!
phrases.notes: The קל וחומר: from the lesser case (earth) to the greater case (Heaven).

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר רבי אסי, דרש רבי שילא איש כפר תמרתא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Draws a broader lesson by קל וחומר from the story in Step 1.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: A Heavenly record of ישראל's merit can never be erased, all the more so than an earthly one.

steps.title: The Servants Spoke From Hatred of המן
steps.stepSummary: On the פסוק "nothing has been done for him," רבא explains that the servants said this because they hated המן, not because they loved מרדכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: "Nothing has been done for him." רבא said: Not because they loved מרדכי, but because they hated המן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and quotes רבא, who explains why the king's servants spoke up.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The servants quickly pointed out that מרדכי was never rewarded. רבא says their motive was not care for מרדכי. They hated המן and were glad for anything that would help his enemy.

keyTerms.meaning: Nothing has been done for him (אסתר ו:ג)

phrases.english: "Nothing has been done for him."
Rava said:
Not because they love Mordecai,
but rather because they hate Haman.

steps.triggerLanguage: לא נעשה עמו דבר. אמר רבא
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in אסתר chapter 6.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The servants' report came from hatred of המן, not love of מרדכי.

steps.title: המן Prepared the Gallows for Himself
steps.stepSummary: A ברייתא reads "הכין לו" (he prepared for him) as "לו הכין": המן really prepared the gallows for himself.
steps.simpleTranslation: "He prepared for him." A ברייתא taught: He prepared it for himself.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes a ברייתא that rereads two words in the פסוק to hint at המן's ending.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The plain meaning is that המן prepared the gallows for מרדכי. The ברייתא reads "לו" as pointing to המן himself. Without knowing it, he was building the gallows on which he would be hanged.

phrases.english: "He had prepared for him."
A baraita taught: For himself he prepared.
phrases.notes: Reversing the word order shows that "לו" refers to המן.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: "לו" refers to המן: the gallows were prepared for his own downfall.

steps.title: המן Asks Which מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: When אחשורוש orders "do so to מרדכי," המן stalls by asking who מרדכי is.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And do so to מרדכי." [המן] said to him: Who is מרדכי?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא begins a back-and-forth between המן and אחשורוש. This step sets up the first move of that conversation.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא explains why the פסוק adds so many descriptions of מרדכי. Each description answers one of המן's excuses. Here המן pretends not to know whom the king means, hoping to escape the order.
steps.confusionAlert: The speakers change with each אמר ליה. המן asks the questions and אחשורוש answers with the words of the פסוק.

phrases.english: "And do so to Mordecai."
[Haman] said to him: Who is Mordecai?

steps.triggerLanguage: ועשה כן למרדכי. אמר ליה: מנו מרדכי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to a new פסוק and begins a dialogue.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which person named מרדכי the king means (a stalling tactic).

steps.title: אחשורוש Answers: The Jew
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש answers with the next word of the פסוק: "היהודי" (the Jew).
steps.simpleTranslation: [אחשורוש] said to him: "The Jew."
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש answers המן's question using the word "היהודי" from the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This explains why the פסוק calls him "מרדכי היהודי." The added word answers המן's first excuse.

phrases.english: [Ahasuerus] said to him: "The Jew."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question in Step 5.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The מרדכי who is the Jew.

steps.title: המן Objects: Many Jews Are Named מרדכי
steps.stepSummary: המן pushes back: there are many men named מרדכי among the Jews.
steps.simpleTranslation: [המן] said to him: There are many named מרדכי among the Jews.
steps.whatsHappening: המן tries a second excuse. He says "the Jew" is still not specific enough.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first answer narrowed it down to Jews, but המן claims that is still unclear. This sets up the need for one more description in the פסוק.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: טוּבָא מָרְדְּכַי אִיכָּא בִּיהוּדָאֵי.
phrases.english: [Haman] said to him: There are many named Mordecai among the Jews.

steps.triggerLanguage: אמר ליה: טובא מרדכי איכא ביהודאי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Challenges the answer given in Step 6.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: Many Jews share the name, so "the Jew" does not pick out one person.

steps.title: אחשורוש Specifies: The One at the King's Gate
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש closes the excuse: the מרדכי "who sits at the king's gate."
steps.simpleTranslation: [אחשורוש] said to him: "The one who sits at the king's gate."
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש answers המן's second excuse with the last description in the פסוק, leaving no way out.
steps.deeperAnalysis: "היושב בשער המלך" points to exactly one person. So every phrase in the פסוק turns out to answer one of המן's attempts to avoid the order.

keyTerms.meaning: Who sits at the king's gate

steps.whatToRemember: The גמרא reads the long description in אסתר ו:י ("מרדכי, the Jew, who sits at the king's gate") as אחשורוש answering המן's excuses one at a time.

phrases.english: [Ahasuerus] said to him: "Who sits at the king's gate."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Resolves the objection in Step 7.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Adds a detail that identifies exactly one person.
steps.terutzHavaAmina: "The Jew" could mean many men named מרדכי.
steps.terutzMaskana: Only one מרדכי sits at the king's gate, so המן has no excuse left.

steps.title: המן tries to swap the honor for a smaller gift
steps.stepSummary: המן suggests that one village or one river would be enough reward for מרדכי.
steps.simpleTranslation: המן said to him: It is enough for him to get one village, or else one river.
steps.whatsHappening: המן has run out of ways to dodge the order. Now he tries to bargain the honor down to a simple material gift.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The earlier steps were stalling about who מרדכי is. This step pushes back on what honor he should get. המן would rather hand over property than publicly parade his enemy.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: סַגִּי לֵיהּ בְּחַד דִּיסְקַרְתָּא,
phrases.english: He (Haman) said to him: It is enough for him with one village,
phrases.notes: דיסקרתא means an estate whose income he would receive.

phrases.english: or else with one river.
phrases.notes: That is, the right to collect taxes from a river.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: After the identity excuse is closed, המן challenges the size of the honor itself.
steps.kashyaTarget: The king's order to give מרדכי the full royal honor.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A smaller material reward would supposedly be enough, so the public honor is not needed.

steps.title: The king insists on everything המן proposed
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש says: give him this too, and do not leave out anything you said.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Give him this too. 'Do not leave out anything from all that you said.'
steps.whatsHappening: אחשורוש rejects the bargain. He says the village or river should be given in addition to everything else.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The גמרא reads the end of the פסוק, 'אל תפל דבר מכל אשר דברת,' as the king's answer to המן's bargaining. Each attempt by המן to shrink the honor only adds to it.

keyTerms.meaning: do not let anything fall away (do not leave anything out)

phrases.aramaic: אָמַר לֵיהּ: הָא נָמֵי הַב לֵיהּ,
phrases.english: He (Ahasuerus) said to him: This too, give him,
phrases.notes: The village or river is added on top of the honor.

phrases.english: 'Let nothing fail of all that you have spoken.'
phrases.notes: Esther 6:10

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This answers המן's attempt to bargain down the honor.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Reading the פסוק as a full rejection of the offer
steps.terutzHavaAmina: המן could replace the honor with a smaller gift.
steps.terutzMaskana: Everything must be given, including המן's new offer.
steps.whatToRemember: Every escape המן tries is closed by the next words of the פסוק.

steps.title: המן finds מרדכי teaching הלכות קמיצה
steps.stepSummary: המן takes the clothes and horse. He finds מרדכי teaching הלכות קמיצה to the חכמים. מרדכי sees him coming with the horse and is afraid.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And המן took the clothing and the horse.' He went and found the חכמים sitting before מרדכי while he showed them the laws of the handful. When מרדכי saw him coming toward him holding the horse, he was afraid.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא now starts a new scene. It quotes the פסוק and tells what happened when המן arrived.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי is in the middle of teaching the laws of קמיצה, the handful of flour taken from a מנחה. This detail sets up המן's conversation with the חכמים in the next steps. מרדכי does not know about the king's order, so he reads המן's arrival as a threat.

keyTerms.meaning: the laws of taking the handful from a מנחה

phrases.english: 'Then Haman took the apparel and the horse.'
phrases.notes: Esther 6:11

phrases.english: He went and found him, with the Sages sitting before him,
and he was demonstrating to the Sages the laws of the handful,
once Mordecai saw him coming out toward him
with the horse held in his hand, he became frightened.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקַּח הָמָן אֶת הַלְּבוּשׁ וְאֶת הַסּוּס
steps.relationToPreviousStep: The king has finished giving orders. The story moves to המן carrying them out.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The פסוק is expanded into a scene: מרדכי is teaching הלכות קמיצה when the frightening המן arrives.

steps.title: מרדכי sends the students away and prays
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי tells the חכמים to leave so they will not be harmed. He wraps himself and prays, and המן sits and waits.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to the חכמים: This wicked man is coming to kill me. Go away from him so you are not burned by his coals. At that moment מרדכי wrapped himself and stood to pray. המן came, sat before them, and waited until מרדכי finished his prayer.
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי expects to die. He protects his students and turns to תפילה, and המן is forced to wait.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי's first reaction to danger is to protect others and to pray. המן, the powerful official, sits and waits for a Jew to finish praying. This waiting time is when the next conversation happens.

keyTerms.meaning: so you will not be burned by his coal (harmed by him)

steps.confusionAlert: Some of the students may have stayed, because in the next step המן speaks to people sitting there ('אמר להו'). Do not assume everyone left.

phrases.english: He said to the Sages:

phrases.aramaic: הַאי רַשִּׁיעָא לְמִיקְטַל נַפְשַׁי קָא אָתֵי
phrases.english: This wicked man is coming to kill me;

phrases.aramaic: זִילוּ מִקַּמֵּיהּ דִּי לָא תִּכָּווּ בְּגַחַלְתּוֹ.
phrases.english: go away from before him so that you will not be burned by his coals.

phrases.aramaic: בְּהָהִיא שַׁעְתָּא נִתְעַטֵּף מָרְדְּכַי וְקָם לֵיהּ לִצְלוֹתָא,
phrases.english: At that moment Mordecai wrapped himself and stood up to pray;
Haman came and sat down before them
and waited until Mordecai finished his prayer.

steps.triggerLanguage: הַאי רַשִּׁיעָא לְמִיקְטַל נַפְשַׁי קָא אָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This continues the scene with מרדכי's reaction to his fear.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרדכי sends his students away from danger and prays, while המן waits.

steps.title: המן asks what they were studying
steps.stepSummary: While waiting, המן asks the חכמים what they were busy with.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: What were you busy with?
steps.whatsHappening: המן asks a simple question to pass the time. It sets up the answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This is a real question asking for information. It brings the topic of קמיצה back into the story, so the גמרא can show what that learning achieved.

phrases.english: He said to them: With what were you occupied?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: המן uses the waiting time to question the students.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What topic the חכמים were learning.

steps.title: The חכמים explain the handful from a מנחה
steps.stepSummary: They explain that when the בית המקדש stood, a person who pledged a מנחה brought a handful of fine flour and gained כפרה.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: When the בית המקדש stands, a person who pledges a מנחה brings a handful of fine flour and receives atonement.
steps.whatsHappening: The חכמים answer המן's question with the basic idea of קמיצה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The point is how small the offering is: just a fistful of flour, and yet it brings כפרה. This sets up המן's bitter reaction in the next step.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: בִּזְמַן שֶׁבֵּית הַמִּקְדָּשׁ קַיָּים,
phrases.english: They said to him: When the Temple is standing,
one who pledges a meal-offering

phrases.aramaic: מַיְיתֵי מְלֵי קוּמְצֵיהּ דְּסוּלְתָּא וּמִתְכַּפַּר לֵיהּ.
phrases.english: brings a full handful of fine flour and achieves atonement.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: This directly answers המן's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They were learning about the handful of flour from a מנחה, which brings atonement.

steps.title: המן admits the handful beat his silver
steps.stepSummary: המן says their handful of flour has come and pushed aside his ten thousand talents of silver.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to them: Your handful of flour came and pushed away my ten thousand talents of silver.
steps.whatsHappening: המן realizes why his plan collapsed and says it out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Earlier in the מגילה, המן offered ten thousand כיכר of silver to destroy the Jews. He now admits that a tiny amount of תורה learning and עבודה outweighed his huge bribe.
steps.whyThisMatters: This is the turning point of the story. The power of a small מצוה and תורה learning defeats המן's money.
steps.whatToRemember: A handful of flour, through תורה learning about it, outweighed ten thousand talents of silver.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לְהוּ: אֲתָא מְלֵי קוּמְצֵי קִמְחָא דִּידְכוּ
phrases.english: He said to them: Your full handful of flour has come

phrases.aramaic: וְדָחֵי עַשְׂרָה אַלְפֵי כַּכְּרֵי כַסְפָּא דִּידִי.
phrases.english: and pushed aside my ten thousand talents of silver.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: המן reacts to the חכמים' answer.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן admits that the handful of flour defeated his silver.

steps.title: מרדכי: a slave's property belongs to his master
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי, finished praying, calls המן wicked. He asks: when a slave buys property, who owns the slave and who owns the property?
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wicked one! A slave who bought property: whose is the slave, and whose is the property?
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי attacks המן's claim that the silver was 'mine.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: There is a tradition that המן once sold himself as a slave to מרדכי. A slave's property belongs to his master, so the silver was never really המן's to give. מרדכי's question is rhetorical and works as a sharp challenge.
steps.confusionAlert: This is not a halachic question about slaves. It is a jab: המן is מרדכי's slave, so 'my silver' is really מרדכי's.

phrases.english: He (Mordecai) said to him: Wicked one,
a slave who bought property,
to whom belongs the slave, and to whom belongs the property?

steps.triggerLanguage: עֶבֶד שֶׁקָּנָה נְכָסִים, עֶבֶד לְמִי וּנְכָסִים לְמִי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This targets the word 'דידי' (my) in המן's statement.
steps.kashyaTarget: המן's claim that the ten thousand talents were his own.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: A slave owns nothing apart from his master. המן is מרדכי's slave, so the silver was never his.

steps.title: המן delivers the king's order
steps.stepSummary: המן tells מרדכי to get up, put on the garments, and ride the horse, because the king wants him.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Get up, put on these clothes and ride this horse, because the king wants you.
steps.whatsHappening: המן finally carries out the king's command and tells מרדכי about the honor.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only now do we learn that מרדכי's fear was mistaken. המן came to honor him, not to kill him.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: קוּם לְבוֹשׁ הָנֵי מָאנֵי
phrases.english: He (Haman) said to him: Stand up, put on these garments

phrases.aramaic: וּרְכוֹב הַאי סוּסְיָא, דְּבָעֵי לָךְ מַלְכָּא.
phrases.english: and ride this horse, for the king wants you.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: The story returns to the main mission begun in step 11.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן tells מרדכי about the king's order.

steps.title: מרדכי must first bathe and cut his hair
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי says he cannot, until he goes to the bathhouse and trims his hair. It is not proper to use the king's clothes in this state.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I cannot, until I go into the bathhouse and cut my hair, because it is not proper to use the king's clothes like this.
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי answers המן's order with a condition. He must clean up first out of respect for the king's garments.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי had been fasting and mourning, so he was unkempt. Proper דרך ארץ requires him to be clean before wearing royal clothing. This sets up the next part of the story about who will do the bathing and haircut.

phrases.english: He (Mordecai) said to him: I cannot,

phrases.aramaic: עַד דְּעָיֵילְנָא לְבֵי בָנֵי וְאֶשְׁקוֹל לְמַזְיָיא,
phrases.english: until I enter the bathhouse and trim my hair,
for it is not proper conduct
to use the king's garments like this.

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא יָכֵילְנָא עַד דְּעָיֵילְנָא לְבֵי בָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: This responds to המן's command and delays carrying it out.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He will wear the garments only after bathing and cutting his hair, out of respect for royal clothing.

steps.title: אסתר closes the bathhouses, so המן must wash and trim מרדכי himself
steps.stepSummary: אסתר shuts every bathhouse and barbershop. המן is forced to bathe מרדכי and cut his hair with his own hands.
steps.simpleTranslation: אסתר sent messengers and closed all the bathhouses and all the craftsmen's shops. So המן himself brought מרדכי into the bathhouse and washed him. Then he went, brought scissors from his house, and trimmed his hair.
steps.whatsHappening: The story moves forward: מרדכי said he must bathe and get a haircut first, so אסתר makes sure nobody else is available and המן has to do it himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the last step, מרדכי demanded a bath and haircut before he would wear the king's clothes. אסתר closes every shop, which leaves המן no way out. The great minister is reduced to doing a servant's job.

phrases.english: Esther sent and closed
all the bathhouses
and all the craftsmen.
phrases.notes: This means barbers and bloodletters.

phrases.english: He himself brought him into the bathhouse and washed him,
and he went and brought scissors from his house
and was trimming his hair with them.

steps.triggerLanguage: שַׁדַּרָה אֶסְתֵּר וַאֲסַרְתִּינְהוּ לְכוּלְּהוּ בֵּי בָנֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows how מרדכי's demand for a bath and haircut gets fulfilled.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Because אסתר closed every shop, המן personally bathed מרדכי and trimmed his hair.

steps.title: המן cuts himself and sighs, and מרדכי asks why
steps.stepSummary: While cutting מרדכי's hair, המן injures himself and groans. מרדכי asks him why he is sighing.
steps.simpleTranslation: While he was trimming his hair, המן injured himself and sighed. מרדכי said to him: Why are you sighing?
steps.whatsHappening: המן hurts himself and groans. מרדכי's question sets up המן's complaint in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The sigh shows how much המן feels the humiliation. מרדכי's question opens a short exchange in which המן reveals his self-pity.

phrases.english: While he was trimming him
he injured himself and sighed.
He (Mordechai) said to him: Why are you sighing?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the haircut scene.

steps.title: המן complains that the king's top minister has become a bath attendant and barber
steps.stepSummary: המן answers that he, once the king's most important minister, has been turned into a bathhouse attendant and a barber.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: The man the king regarded above all his ministers is now made into a bathhouse attendant and a barber?
steps.whatsHappening: המן explains his sigh: he feels terribly degraded.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן contrasts his high rank with the lowly job he is doing now. This sets up מרדכי's cutting reply.

phrases.aramaic: אֲמַר לֵיהּ: גַּבְרָא דַּהֲוָה חֲשִׁיב לֵיהּ
phrases.english: He said to him: The man who was considered important to
the king above all his ministers,
now he should be made a bath attendant and a barber?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers מרדכי's question.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He sighs because he went from top minister to bath attendant and barber.

steps.title: מרדכי reminds המן he used to be a village barber
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי calls המן wicked and says: weren't you the barber of כפר קרצום? You have simply gone back to your old job.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Wicked one, weren't you the barber of כפר קרצום?
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי rejects המן's self-pity.
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן claims that barbering is beneath him. מרדכי answers that it is his original trade, so there is nothing new to complain about.

phrases.english: He said to him: Wicked one,

phrases.aramaic: וְלָאו סַפָּר שֶׁל כְּפַר קַרְצוּם הָיִיתָ?
phrases.english: were you not the barber of the village of Kartzum?

steps.triggerLanguage: רָשָׁע, וְלָאו סַפָּר שֶׁל כְּפַר קַרְצוּם הָיִיתָ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Rejects המן's complaint.
steps.dechiyaRejectionScope: המן's claim that barbering degrades him.
steps.dechiyaFlawIdentified: He was a barber before he rose to power.

steps.title: A ברייתא confirms המן was a barber for twenty-two years
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא brings a ברייתא: המן was the barber of כפר קרצום for 22 years.
steps.simpleTranslation: It was taught: המן was the barber of כפר קרצום for twenty-two years.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up מרדכי's remark with a ברייתא.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי's insult is not just name-calling. The ברייתא confirms it is a historical fact about המן's past.

phrases.aramaic: תָּנָא: הָמָן, סַפָּר שֶׁל כְּפַר קַרְצוּם
phrases.english: It was taught: Haman was the barber of the village of Kartzum
for twenty-two years.

steps.triggerLanguage: תָּנָא: הָמָן, סַפָּר שֶׁל כְּפַר קַרְצוּם
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Supports מרדכי's statement.

steps.title: המן dresses מרדכי and tells him to mount the horse
steps.stepSummary: After the haircut, המן dresses מרדכי in the royal clothes and tells him to get up and ride.
steps.simpleTranslation: After he trimmed his hair, he dressed him in his garments. He said to him: Go up and ride.
steps.whatsHappening: The story continues with the next stage of the honor ceremony, and this sets up מרדכי's reply.
steps.deeperAnalysis: מרדכי's condition from the last section has now been met. המן moves on to putting him on the horse.

phrases.english: After he trimmed his hair,
he dressed him in the garments,
He said to him: Mount and ride.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Next stage of the ceremony.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן dresses מרדכי and orders him to ride.

steps.title: מרדכי is too weak from fasting to climb up
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי says he cannot climb up, because his strength is drained from the days of fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: I can't, because my strength is weak from the days of fasting.
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי answers המן's order with another obstacle, and this sets up the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The fasting refers to the תעניות observed for the Jewish people. It also explains why המן ends up having to bend down.

phrases.english: He said to him: I am unable,
because my strength is weakened from the days of fasting.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers המן's order.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: He is too weak from fasting to mount the horse.

steps.title: המן bends down, and מרדכי climbs on him and kicks him
steps.stepSummary: המן stoops so מרדכי can climb up using him, and as מרדכי goes up he kicks המן.
steps.simpleTranslation: He bent down and he climbed up. As he went up, he kicked him.
steps.whatsHappening: המן serves as a step for מרדכי, who kicks him on the way up. This sets up המן's objection.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The humiliation now becomes physical. The kick leads directly to a discussion of whether it was proper.

phrases.english: He (Haman) bent down and he (Mordechai) climbed up.
As he climbed up, he kicked him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Result of מרדכי's weakness.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרדכי climbs up using המן and kicks him.

steps.title: המן objects: your own תורה forbids rejoicing at an enemy's fall
steps.stepSummary: המן challenges מרדכי with a פסוק from משלי: don't rejoice when your enemy falls.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: Isn't it written for you: 'When your enemy falls, do not rejoice'?
steps.whatsHappening: המן uses the Jews' own פסוק to attack מרדכי's kick.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The challenge is that kicking a fallen enemy seems to break an explicit instruction in תנ"ך.

keyTerms.meaning: When your enemy falls, do not rejoice (משלי כד:יז)

phrases.english: He said to him: Is it not written for you:
"When your enemy falls, do not rejoice"?

steps.triggerLanguage: לָא כְּתִיב לְכוּ: בִּנְפֹל אוֹיִבְךָ אַל תִּשְׂמָח
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Objects to the kick.
steps.kashyaTarget: מרדכי's kicking and rejoicing over המן.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: The פסוק in משלי forbids rejoicing at an enemy's downfall.

steps.title: מרדכי answers: that פסוק is about Jews, but about you it says we will tread on you
steps.stepSummary: מרדכי limits the פסוק in משלי to a Jewish enemy. About המן's people, the Torah says 'you shall tread upon their high places.'
steps.simpleTranslation: He said to him: That applies to a Jew, but regarding you it is written: 'And you shall tread upon their high places.'
steps.whatsHappening: מרדכי answers המן's challenge by limiting the scope of the פסוק.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The ban on rejoicing applies to a Jewish enemy. For an enemy like המן's nation, the פסוק in דברים describes trampling them. So the kick does not contradict the פסוק.

keyTerms.meaning: And you shall tread upon their high places (דברים לג:כט)

steps.whatToRemember: The פסוק 'בִּנְפֹל אוֹיִבְךָ' is limited to a fellow Jew. Against an enemy like המן's people, 'עַל בָּמוֹתֵימוֹ תִדְרוֹךְ' applies.

phrases.english: He said to him: This applies to a Jew,
but regarding you it is written:
"And you shall tread upon their high places."

steps.triggerLanguage: הָנֵי מִילֵּי בְּיִשְׂרָאֵל, אֲבָל בְּדִידְכוּ כְּתִיב
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers המן's challenge.
steps.terutzResolutionType: Limiting the scope of the פסוק
steps.terutzHavaAmina: The פסוק forbids rejoicing over any enemy.
steps.terutzMaskana: It applies to a Jewish enemy. Against המן's people one may 'tread upon their high places.'

steps.title: During the parade, המן's daughter dumps a chamber pot on her father by mistake
steps.stepSummary: While המן leads מרדכי past his own house, his daughter on the roof thinks the rider is her father and the man walking is מרדכי. She throws a chamber pot onto the walker's head, which is actually המן's.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And he proclaimed before him: So shall be done to the man the king wishes to honor.' As he was leading him along the street of המן's house, his daughter, standing on the roof, saw it. She assumed the rider was her father and the one walking before him was מרדכי. She took a chamber pot and threw it onto her father's head.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the פסוק of the proclamation and adds a story of what happened along the route.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The daughter expected her father to be honored, so she reversed the two men in her mind. Her attempt to humiliate מרדכי lands on המן instead.

keyTerms.meaning: Who walks in front of him

phrases.english: "And he proclaimed before him: Thus shall be done
to the man whom the king desires to honor."
As he was leading him along
on the street of Haman's house,
his daughter, who was standing on the roof, saw him,
she thought: this one who is riding is her father,
and this one walking before him is Mordechai.
She took a chamber pot
and threw it on her father's head.

steps.triggerLanguage: וַיִּקְרָא לְפָנָיו כָּכָה יֵעָשֶׂה לְאִישׁ אֲשֶׁר הַמֶּלֶךְ חָפֵץ בִּיקָרוֹ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves from mounting the horse to the parade itself.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן's daughter mistakenly humiliated her own father.

steps.title: The daughter sees it was her father and falls to her death
steps.stepSummary: המן looks up, his daughter realizes it was her father, and she falls from the roof and dies.
steps.simpleTranslation: He raised his eyes and she saw that it was her father. She fell from the roof to the ground and died.
steps.whatsHappening: The daughter story ends tragically for המן's family.
steps.deeperAnalysis: This death prepares the explanation in step 32 of why המן was 'mourning.'

phrases.english: He raised his eyes, and she saw that it was her father,
she fell from the roof to the ground and died.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Outcome of the daughter's mistake.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The daughter fell and died.

steps.title: רב ששת: מרדכי returned to his sackcloth and fasting
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא links the story to the פסוק 'וַיָּשָׁב מָרְדֳּכַי אֶל שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ.' רב ששת explains that מרדכי went back to his sackcloth and fasting.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'And מרדכי returned to the king's gate.' רב ששת said: He returned to his sackcloth and his fasting.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא connects the story back to the פסוקים and explains מרדכי's reaction.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Even after his great honor, מרדכי did not celebrate, because the decree against the Jews still stood. 'Returned' means he went back to his mourning and prayer.

keyTerms.meaning: And this is what is written

steps.whyThisMatters: מרדכי's personal honor did not distract him from the danger facing כלל ישראל.

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"And Mordechai returned to the king's gate,"
Rav Sheshet said:
that he returned to his sackcloth and his fasting.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהַיְינוּ דִּכְתִיב: וַיָּשׇׁב מׇרְדֳּכַי אֶל שַׁעַר הַמֶּלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Ties the story back to the text of the מגילה.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: מרדכי returned to sackcloth and fasting.

steps.title: המן mourns his daughter and covers his filthy head
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says המן hurried home 'mourning and with his head covered.' The mourning was for his daughter, and the covered head was because of what happened to him.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And המן hurried to his house, mourning and with his head covered.' 'Mourning': over his daughter. 'With his head covered': because of what happened to him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא reads each word of the פסוק as a reference to the story it just told.
steps.deeperAnalysis: 'אָבֵל' refers to his daughter's death. 'חֲפוּי רֹאשׁ' refers to the filth dumped on his head. Each word of the פסוק is explained by a separate event.
steps.whatToRemember: The day ends with מרדכי back in prayer and fasting, while המן is humiliated and grieving: a mourner over his daughter, with his head covered in filth.

phrases.english: "And Haman hurried to his house
mourning and with his head covered."
"Mourning": over his daughter,
"and with his head covered": over what happened to him.

steps.triggerLanguage: וְהָמָן נִדְחַף אֶל בֵּיתוֹ אָבֵל וַחֲפוּי רֹאשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Contrasts המן's reaction with מרדכי's.
steps.maskanaFinalTakeaway: המן mourned his daughter and covered his head because of the filth thrown on it.

steps.title: Friends or wise men?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק first calls המן's people 'his friends' and then 'his wise men.' The גמרא notices the change of name.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And המן told זרש his wife and all his friends, etc." It calls them 'his friends,' and then it calls them 'his wise men.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק and points out that the same people get two different names. This sets up רבי יוחנן's explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In the same פסוק, המן's circle is first called אוהביו (his friends) and then חכמיו (his wise men). Why would the פסוק upgrade them to 'wise'? The question is implied, not stated outright.

phrases.english: "And Haman recounted to Zeresh his wife
and to all his friends, etc."
phrases.notes: Esther 6:13. The rest of the פסוק calls them 'his wise men.'

phrases.english: It calls them "his friends"
and it calls them "his wise men."

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story right after המן returns home mourning (Step 32) and moves on to the next פסוק.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why does the פסוק switch from 'friends' to 'wise men'?

steps.title: Anyone who says something wise is called wise
steps.stepSummary: רבי יוחנן explains that whoever says a wise thing, even a non-Jew, is called a חכם.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי יוחנן said: Anyone who says something wise, even among the nations of the world, is called a wise man.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי יוחנן answers why המן's friends are suddenly called 'wise men.' They said something wise, so the פסוק gives them that title.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The new name is earned by the words they are about to say, which are the advice in the rest of the פסוק. Being a non-Jew does not stop someone from being called wise. The next steps show what that wise remark was.

phrases.english: Rabbi Yochanan said:
Whoever says something wise,
even among the nations of the world,
is called a wise man.

steps.whyThisMatters: This is a general principle about the Torah's view of wisdom. Wisdom is recognized wherever it is found.
steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי יוֹחָנָן: כׇּל הָאוֹמֵר דְּבַר חָכְמָה
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the implied question of Step 33.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: They are called wise because they said something wise. Anyone who does so, even a non-Jew, earns the title.

steps.title: Which tribes המן cannot defeat
steps.stepSummary: The advisors' wise remark: if מרדכי comes from יהודה, בנימין, אפרים, or מנשה, המן cannot win. From any other שבט, he can.
steps.simpleTranslation: "If מרדכי is of the seed of the Jews, etc." They said to him: If he comes from the other tribes, you can beat him. But if he is from the tribe of יהודה, בנימין, אפרים, or מנשה, you cannot beat him.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא explains what the 'wise' advice actually meant. The word יהודים is read as hinting at specific שבטים that המן cannot overcome.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The advisors did not say המן loses to every Jew. They drew a distinction: most שבטים can be defeated, but four special ones cannot. Being this precise is what made their words 'wise.'

keyTerms.meaning: From the seed of the Jews

steps.confusionAlert: מרדכי was from שבט בנימין, so he fits one of the four 'undefeatable' שבטים.

phrases.english: "If Mordecai is of the seed of the Jews, etc."
They said to him:
If he comes from the other tribes,
you can overpower him,

phrases.aramaic: וְאִי מִשֵּׁבֶט יְהוּדָה וּבִנְיָמִין וְאֶפְרַיִם וּמְנַשֶּׁה —
phrases.english: but if from the tribe of Judah, Benjamin, Ephraim, or Manasseh,
you cannot overpower him.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֲמַרוּ לֵיהּ: אִי מִשְּׁאָר שְׁבָטִים קָאָתֵי
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Shows the content of the wise remark that earned them the title 'wise men.'
steps.mimraCoreRuling: המן can defeat descendants of most שבטים, but not those of יהודה, בנימין, אפרים, or מנשה.

steps.title: Verses proving these tribes win
steps.stepSummary: A פסוק in בראשית proves that יהודה wins. A פסוק in תהלים proves the same for אפרים, בנימין, and מנשה.
steps.simpleTranslation: יהודה, as it is written: "Your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies." The others, as it is written about them: "Before אפרים and בנימין and מנשה, stir up Your might."
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא backs up the advisors' claim with פסוקים. It gives one source for יהודה and another for the other three שבטים.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יעקב's ברכה to יהודה says his hand will be on his enemies' neck, meaning he defeats them. The פסוק in תהלים asks ה׳ to show His strength 'before' אפרים, בנימין, and מנשה, meaning ה׳ fights for them. Together they cover all four שבטים named in Step 35.

phrases.english: Judah, as it is written:
"Your hand shall be on the neck of your enemies,"
phrases.notes: Genesis 49:8

phrases.english: The others, as it is written about them:
"Before Ephraim and Benjamin and Manasseh
stir up Your might."
phrases.notes: Psalms 80:3

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Provides the scriptural basis for the four-tribe claim in Step 35.
steps.raayaObject: That יהודה, בנימין, אפרים, and מנשה cannot be defeated.
steps.raayaSupportSource: Genesis 49:8 for יהודה, and Psalms 80:3 for אפרים, בנימין, and מנשה.

steps.title: Why the double 'falling'?
steps.stepSummary: רבי יהודה בר אלעאי asks why the פסוק uses two forms of 'fall' (נפול תפול).
steps.simpleTranslation: "You will surely fall before him." רבי יהודה בר אלעאי expounded: Why these two fallings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the end of the advisors' words and points out the doubled verb. This sets up the explanation in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק could have just said 'you will fall,' but it says נפול תפול, 'falling you will fall.' רבי יהודה בר אלעאי treats the extra word as a hint that needs explaining.

keyTerms.meaning: You will surely fall (literally 'falling you will fall')

phrases.english: "You will surely fall before him."
Rabbi Yehuda bar Ilai expounded:
Why these two fallings?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next words of the same advice from המן's advisors.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What does the doubled verb נפול תפול add?

steps.title: The Jews are like dust and like stars
steps.stepSummary: The advisors told המן that the Jewish people are compared to both dust and stars. When they fall, they fall to the dust, and when they rise, they rise to the stars.
steps.simpleTranslation: They said to him: This nation is compared to dust and compared to stars. When they go down, they go down to the dust. When they go up, they go up to the stars.
steps.whatsHappening: This answers why the 'fall' is doubled. Now that מרדכי is rising, he will rise all the way, so המן will fall completely.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The Jews are compared to dust and to stars because their situation goes to extremes. Once מרדכי has started rising, there is no middle ground, and המן's fall will be total. That is what the double wording expresses.
steps.whatToRemember: The advisors' 'wisdom' was recognizing two things: the special שבטים cannot be beaten, and the Jewish people swing between extremes. Once מרדכי began to rise, המן's total fall was certain.

phrases.english: They said to him:
phrases.notes: Still part of רבי יהודה בר אלעאי's explanation. 'They' are המן's advisors.

phrases.english: This nation is compared to dust
and compared to stars.
When they descend, they descend to the dust,
and when they rise, they rise to the stars.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרוּ לוֹ: אוּמָּה זוֹ, מְשׁוּלָה לְעָפָר
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of Step 37.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The double 'fall' reflects that the Jews go to extremes: down to the dust or up to the stars. Since מרדכי is rising, המן will fall completely.

steps.title: המן is rushed to the feast
steps.stepSummary: The king's servants 'ויבהילו,' meaning they brought המן in a panicked rush.
steps.simpleTranslation: "And the king's chamberlains arrived and hurried." This teaches that they brought him in a panic.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא moves to the next פסוק and explains the word ויבהילו. It means המן was dragged off in a confused rush.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The word ויבהילו comes from בהלה, which means panic or disarray. Some explain that this means he was not even given a chance to clean himself from the filth his daughter had dropped on him (Step 29). His humiliation continues right up to אסתר's feast.

phrases.english: "And the king's chamberlains arrived and hurried."
phrases.notes: Esther 6:14

phrases.english: This teaches that they brought him in a panic.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves to the next פסוק after the advisors' warning.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: ויבהילו means the servants rushed המן to the feast in disarray, with no time to compose or clean himself.

steps.title: אסתר tells the king that המן keeps harming him
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא reads 'אין הצר שוה בנזק המלך' as אסתר's charge that המן does not care about hurting the king. He had ושתי killed, and now he wants to kill אסתר.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'For we are sold, I and my people... for the enemy is not worth the damage to the king.' She said to him: This enemy does not care about the damage he does to the king. He was jealous of ושתי and had her killed, and now he is jealous of me and wants to kill me.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אסתר's words to the king and explains what she really meant. She was warning him that המן is a danger to the king himself.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple reading of the פסוק is that the trouble 'is not worth' bothering the king. The גמרא instead reads 'אינו שוה בנזק המלך' as 'he doesn't care about the king's loss.' This turns אסתר's plea into a personal warning: המן already cost the king one queen (ושתי) and is about to cost him a second.

keyTerms.meaning: The damage or loss to the king
The previous queen, who was killed

steps.confusionAlert: The claim that המן was behind ושתי's death relies on an earlier דרשה in the גמרא that ממוכן, who advised killing ושתי, was המן.

phrases.english: 'For we are sold, I and my people, etc.'
phrases.notes: Esther 7:4

phrases.aramaic: כִּי אֵין הַצָּר שֹׁוֶה בְּנֵזֶק הַמֶּלֶךְ״.
phrases.english: 'for the enemy is not worth the damage to the king.'

phrases.aramaic: אָמְרָה לוֹ: צַר זֶה, אֵינוֹ שֹׁוֶה בְּנֵזֶק שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ.
phrases.english: She said to him: This enemy does not care about the damage to the king.
phrases.notes: This is the גמרא's new way of reading the פסוק.

phrases.english: He was jealous of Vashti and killed her,
now he is jealous of me and wants to kill me.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמְרָה לוֹ: צַר זֶה, אֵינוֹ שֹׁוֶה בְּנֵזֶק שֶׁל מֶלֶךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the line-by-line reading of מגילת אסתר, moving forward to אסתר's accusation at the second feast.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: 'אין הצר שוה בנזק המלך' means המן does not care about the harm he causes the king: he had ושתי killed and now seeks אסתר's death.

steps.title: Why does the verse say 'and he said' twice?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes a פסוק where 'ויאמר' appears twice in a row and asks why the repetition is needed.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And King אחשורוש said, and he said to אסתר המלכה.' Why do I need 'he said' and again 'he said'?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא spots an extra word in the פסוק and asks why it is there. This step sets up רבי אבהו's answer in the next step.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Saying 'ויאמר' once would be enough to tell us the king spoke. Since the תורה does not waste words, the second 'ויאמר' must be teaching something new about how he spoke.

keyTerms.meaning: Why do I need it? (asking about an extra word)

phrases.english: 'And King Ahasuerus said,'
phrases.notes: Esther 7:5

phrases.english: 'and he said to Queen Esther.'
Why do I need 'he said' and again 'he said'?

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק and raises a question about its wording.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: What extra meaning the doubled 'ויאמר' carries.

steps.title: First through a translator, then directly
steps.stepSummary: רבי אבהו explains that the king first spoke to אסתר through a translator. Once she told him she came from בית שאול, he spoke to her directly.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אבהו said: At first he spoke to her through a translator. Once she told him, 'I come from the family of שאול,' right away the פסוק says, 'and he said to אסתר המלכה' (he spoke to her himself).
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אבהו answers the question about the double 'ויאמר.' Each 'ויאמר' stands for a different way the king spoke to her.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The first 'ויאמר' was indirect speech, through a translator, because the king thought אסתר came from a common family. The second 'ויאמר,' addressed to 'אסתר המלכה,' shows him speaking to her himself. That changed once he learned she came from royal blood, the house of שאול המלך.

keyTerms.meaning: Translator / interpreter who speaks on someone's behalf
From the house (family) of King Saul

phrases.english: Rabbi Abbahu said:
At first, through a translator,
once she told him
'I come from the house of Saul,'
immediately: 'and he said to Queen Esther.'
phrases.notes: Now he spoke to her directly

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֲבָהוּ: בַּתְּחִלָּה עַל יְדֵי תּוּרְגְּמָן
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers the question of step 41.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The first 'ויאמר' was through a translator. The second shows the king speaking directly to אסתר after he learned of her royal lineage from שאול.

steps.title: אסתר pointed at the king, but a מלאך moved her hand
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that when אסתר said 'an enemy and foe,' she was really pointing at אחשורוש, and a מלאך pushed her hand toward המן.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And אסתר said: An enemy and foe is this wicked המן.' רבי אלעזר said: This teaches that she was pointing toward אחשורוש, and a מלאך came and pushed her hand toward המן.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes אסתר's famous accusation. רבי אלעזר adds a hidden detail about what really happened as she said it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The words 'צר ואויב' (enemy and foe) are said before the name 'המן,' which allows a reading that her gesture first went to the king, who had in fact agreed to the decree. A מלאך redirected her hand so that the king's anger would fall on המן and not on her.

phrases.english: 'And Esther said: An enemy and foe'
phrases.notes: Esther 7:6

phrases.english: 'is this wicked Haman.'
Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that she was pointing toward Ahasuerus,

phrases.aramaic: וּבָא מַלְאָךְ וְסָטַר יָדָהּ כְּלַפֵּי הָמָן.
phrases.english: and an angel came and pushed her hand toward Haman.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁהָיְתָה מַחְווֹה כְּלַפֵּי אֲחַשְׁוֵרוֹשׁ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: אסתר's gesture was aimed at אחשורוש, and a מלאך redirected it to המן.

steps.title: The king left angry and came back angry
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא compares the king's rising and going out to the garden with his return from it: both happened in anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the king rose in his anger, etc.' and 'the king returned from the palace garden.' The פסוק compares his returning to his rising: just as his rising was in anger, so too his returning was in anger.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא puts two פסוקים side by side and learns from one to the other. This step also sets up the next step, which explains why the king was still angry when he came back.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Only the rising says 'בחמתו' (in his anger), but the parallel wording links the two actions. This tells us the king's anger did not cool off in the garden. That raises an obvious question: what kept him angry? The next step answers it.

keyTerms.meaning: Compares (links two things so one teaches about the other)

phrases.english: 'And the king rose in his anger, etc.'
phrases.notes: Esther 7:7

phrases.english: 'And the king returned from the palace garden.'
phrases.notes: Esther 7:8

phrases.english: It compares the returning to the rising:
just as the rising was in anger,
so too the returning was in anger.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוקים in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: Through a היקש, the king's return from the garden was in anger, just like his leaving.

steps.title: Angels disguised as men uproot the king's trees
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא explains why the king came back angry. In the garden he found מלאכי השרת, looking like men, cutting down his trees, and they claimed המן had ordered it.
steps.simpleTranslation: For he went out and found מלאכי השרת who looked to him like men, and they were uprooting the trees of the garden. He said to them: What are you doing? They said to him: המן commanded us.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא tells a short story explaining why the king's anger did not cool off in the garden. It answers the question raised in Step 44.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Step 44 taught that the king returned still angry. This story gives the reason: he saw his own trees being destroyed, apparently on המן's orders. That added a fresh reason to be furious at המן, right before he came back in and found המן fallen on אסתר's couch.
steps.whatToRemember: In this section the גמרא shows heaven working behind the scenes to turn אחשורוש against המן. A מלאך moves אסתר's hand toward המן, and מלאכים disguised as men make it look as if המן is destroying the king's garden.

phrases.english: For he went and found ministering angels
who appeared to him like men,
and they were uprooting the trees of the garden,
and he said to them: What are you doing?
They said to him: Haman commanded us.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Explains the reason behind the king's continued anger established in step 44.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king returned angry because מלאכים disguised as men were uprooting his trees and claimed המן had ordered it.

steps.title: Why does the פסוק say המן 'is falling'?
steps.stepSummary: The king comes back from the garden and finds המן falling on אסתר's couch. The גמרא asks why the פסוק uses 'is falling' (נופל) instead of 'fell' (נפל).
steps.simpleTranslation: He came back to his house, and 'המן is falling on the bed.' Why 'is falling'? It should have said 'fell'!
steps.whatsHappening: The story picks up as the king returns from the garden. The גמרא notices odd wording in the פסוק and asks about it.
steps.deeperAnalysis: נופל describes something still happening, while נפל describes something that already happened. If המן had simply fallen once, the past tense would fit better. So the גמרא senses a hidden message in the present tense.

phrases.english: He (the king) came back to his house,
phrases.notes: He is returning from the garden mentioned in the previous steps.

phrases.english: "and Haman is falling upon the couch" (Esther 7:8),
"Is falling"? It should have said "fell"!
phrases.notes: The question is about the tense of the verb.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Continues the story from the king's angry return from the garden.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Why the פסוק uses the present-tense נופל rather than the past-tense נפל.

steps.title: A מלאך kept pushing המן down
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר explains that a מלאך came and pushed המן down onto the couch, so he kept on falling.
steps.simpleTranslation: רבי אלעזר said: This teaches that an angel came and pushed him down onto it.
steps.whatsHappening: רבי אלעזר answers the question about 'is falling.'
steps.deeperAnalysis: המן was not choosing to lie on אסתר's couch. Each time he tried to get up, the מלאך pushed him back down, which is why the פסוק describes it as still happening. This fits the pattern from earlier steps: מלאכים are quietly arranging המן's downfall.

keyTerms.meaning: pushed him down / made him fall

phrases.english: Rabbi Elazar said:
This teaches that an angel came
and pushed him down upon it (the couch),
phrases.notes: The falling was repeated, so the present tense fits.

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: מְלַמֵּד שֶׁבָּא מַלְאָךְ
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Directly answers the question of step 46.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The present tense shows the falling kept happening, because a מלאך kept pushing המן down.

steps.title: The king's cry: trouble inside and trouble outside
steps.stepSummary: אחשורוש cries 'woe inside the house and woe outside,' and the פסוק records his accusation that המן is attacking the queen.
steps.simpleTranslation: He said: Woe to me inside the house, and woe to me outside! 'And the king said: Will he even force the queen with me in the house?'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא shows how the king reacted: he felt attacked from every direction, and then he accused המן out loud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Outside, the king had found his trees being cut down 'by המן's order' (step 45). Inside, he finds המן on the queen's couch. Both scenes were set up by מלאכים, so to the king it seemed that המן was wronging him everywhere.

phrases.english: He (the king) said: Woe to me inside the house,
and woe to me outside!
phrases.notes: Outside means the garden with the trees being cut down.

phrases.english: "And the king said:
Will he even force the queen
with me in the house?" (Esther 7:8).

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Describes the king's reaction to what the מלאך set up in step 47, tying it back to the garden in step 45.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: The king saw himself as wronged by המן both outside and inside, and that led to his accusation in the פסוק.

steps.title: חרבונה was in on the plot but switched sides
steps.stepSummary: רבי אלעזר teaches that חרבונה was also wicked and part of המן's plan. Once he saw the plan failing, he quickly ran over to the winning side.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And חרבונה said, etc.' רבי אלעזר said: חרבונה was wicked too and part of that plot. As soon as he saw his plot had failed, he immediately ran away from it.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא quotes the next פסוק, where חרבונה points out the gallows. רבי אלעזר reveals the real motive behind what חרבונה said.
steps.deeperAnalysis: We might think חרבונה was a hero for mentioning the gallows. רבי אלעזר says he was actually a partner in the plot to hang מרדכי. He knew about the gallows because he was involved, and he 'informed' only to save himself once המן was clearly falling.

keyTerms.meaning: a royal servant who mentions המן's gallows
fled, ran away (here: abandoned המן's side)

steps.confusionAlert: Do not read 'fled' as running out of the room. It means חרבונה abandoned המן and switched to the winning side.

phrases.english: "And Harbonah said, etc." (Esther 7:9).
Rabbi Elazar said:
Harbonah too was wicked;
he was part of that plot.
Once he saw that his plot had not succeeded,
he immediately fled (from המן's side).

steps.triggerLanguage: אָמַר רַבִּי אֶלְעָזָר: אַף חַרְבוֹנָה רָשָׁע
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק in the story.
steps.mimraCoreRuling: חרבונה was a partner in המן's plot and turned on him only once the plot failed.

steps.title: A פסוק in איוב supports חרבונה's switch
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא supports רבי אלעזר with a פסוק in איוב: when disaster hits a wicked person, even his own friends run from him.
steps.simpleTranslation: And this is what is written: 'It hurls itself at him and does not spare. He tries to flee from its hand.'
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא brings a פסוק from איוב to back up what רבי אלעזר just said about חרבונה.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The פסוק describes punishment falling on a wicked person, with people running away 'from his hand.' This matches חרבונה, who ran away from המן the moment trouble came. It shows that חרבונה's behavior fits a known pattern.

keyTerms.meaning: and this is what is written (a supporting פסוק)

phrases.english: And this is what is written:
"It hurls itself at him and does not spare;
he would surely flee from its hand" (Job 27:22).
phrases.notes: Read here as: the wicked man's friends run from him.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Gives a source for רבי אלעזר's claim in step 49.
steps.raayaObject: That חרבונה abandoned המן once his downfall began.
steps.raayaSupportSource: איוב 27:22, read as: friends run away from a wicked person when disaster strikes him.

steps.title: Why does the word for 'calmed' look doubled?
steps.stepSummary: The פסוק says the king's anger 'calmed' using the word שככה, which has a doubled letter. The גמרא asks why it seems to describe two calmings.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'And the king's anger calmed (שככה).' Why these two calmings?
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא notices that the word שככה repeats the letter כ, as if it describes two calmings, and asks why.
steps.deeperAnalysis: The simple form of the word would have been שכה. The extra כ suggests two different angers calmed at the same moment, and the גמרא wants to know which two.

phrases.english: "And the king's anger calmed" (Esther 7:10).
Why these two calmings?
phrases.notes: Based on the doubled letter in שככה.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Moves on to the next פסוק, after המן is hanged.
steps.sheelahInformationSought: Which two angers the doubled word שככה refers to.

steps.title: God's anger and the king's anger both calmed
steps.stepSummary: First answer: one calming was of the anger of the King of the world (God), and the other was of אחשורוש's anger.
steps.simpleTranslation: One calming was of the King of the world, and one was of אחשורוש.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא gives its first answer about the two calmings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: In מגילה aggadah, 'the king' often hints at God as well. So when המן was hanged, both God's anger at the Jews (from the decree) and the human king's anger at המן settled down together.

keyTerms.meaning: the Persian king in the story

phrases.english: One was the calming of the King of the world,
and one was of Ahasuerus.

steps.relationToPreviousStep: Answers step 51.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: The two calmings were God's anger and אחשורוש's anger.

steps.title: Second answer: anger over אסתר and over ושתי
steps.stepSummary: Another view: both calmings belonged to אחשורוש. One was his anger over אסתר, and the other was his anger over ושתי.
steps.simpleTranslation: And some say: one calming was over אסתר, and one was over ושתי.
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא offers a different answer to the same question about the two calmings.
steps.deeperAnalysis: Here both calmings are the king's, but he had two reasons to be angry at המן. One was what המן did to אסתר. The other went back to ושתי, since (by an earlier מדרש) המן had pushed for her execution. When המן was hanged, both angers settled at once.

phrases.english: And some say:
One was over Esther,
and one was over Vashti.

steps.whatToRemember: The doubled word שככה means two angers calmed together: either God's and the king's, or the king's anger over אסתר and over ושתי.
steps.relationToPreviousStep: A second answer to the same question, offered instead of step 52.
steps.teshuvahAnswerProvided: Both calmings were the king's: one over המן's offense to אסתר, and one over ושתי.

steps.title: How could יוסף favor בנימין after suffering from favoritism?
steps.stepSummary: The גמרא quotes the פסוק where יוסף gives each brother one set of clothes but gives בנימין five. It starts to ask how יוסף could repeat the very favoritism that had caused him so much pain.
steps.simpleTranslation: 'To all of them he gave each man a change of clothes, but to בנימין he gave five changes of clothes.' Is it possible that the very thing that righteous man suffered from...
steps.whatsHappening: The גמרא opens a new topic: a פסוק about יוסף. The question begins here, but the rest of it continues on the next amud.
steps.deeperAnalysis: יוסף's brothers hated him because יעקב favored him with a special coat. So it seems strange that יוסף would now favor בנימין with extra clothes and stir up jealousy again. The answer comes next, and it connects to the מגילה because מרדכי comes from בנימין.
steps.confusionAlert: This sentence is not finished. The rest of the challenge, and its answer, continue on the next amud.

phrases.english: "To all of them he gave each man changes of clothing,
but to Benjamin he gave five changes of clothing" (Genesis 45:22).

phrases.aramaic: אֶפְשָׁר דָּבָר שֶׁנִּצְטַעֵר בּוֹ אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק —
phrases.english: Is it possible that the very thing from which that righteous man suffered...
phrases.notes: That is, favoritism. The sentence continues on the next amud.

steps.triggerLanguage: אֶפְשָׁר דָּבָר שֶׁנִּצְטַעֵר בּוֹ אוֹתוֹ צַדִּיק
steps.relationToPreviousStep: Breaks away from the אסתר story to discuss a related פסוק about יוסף.
steps.kashyaTarget: The behavior of יוסף described in בראשית 45:22.
steps.kashyaAttackLogic: יוסף suffered from his brothers' jealousy over favoritism, so how could he give בנימין extra gifts and risk the same jealousy?
